plan.goal: Determine the number of biological replicates per group needed to detect a 0.5-sigma difference between two groups with 80% power at alpha 0.05 (two-sided).
plan.rationale: This is a pure power-analysis design. The effect size is 0.5 standard deviations (effect_size = 0.5, std_dev = 1.0 in the same units), with the standard defaults of alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8, and a two-sided two-sample t-test. The sample size per group is computed by the calculator from these raw inputs; no derived n is supplied.
caveats: 63 replicates per group is a large commitment; confirm the platform (chips/wells) can accommodate ~126 total biological replicates plus technical replicates and controls.
A 0.5-sigma effect is small; verify the effect size is biologically meaningful and that assay variability (sigma) is well characterized before committing.
If 63/group is not feasible, the study will be underpowered and risks a false negative — consider a larger effect size or accept lower power.

provenance.formula: n from two-sample t-test power equation
